abstracted_dimensions: twenty-four lighting and color vocabulary families
source quality direction role portrait pattern shadow highlight tone color optics postprocess and film terms
twelve example combinations spanning beauty editorial cinematic natural-light filmic and direct-flash looks
research_limitations: the referenced conversation is a vocabulary map rather than an authoritative technical source
a term list does not prove that each term owns a stable single-frame visual contract
reuse_note: Use the taxonomy to define research coverage, then require an independent source and observable relation before hard-profile promotion.

abstracted_dimensions: relative physical source size and diffusion determine hard or soft shadow-edge transfer rather than intensity alone
key fill separation and background are functional roles
diffused value specular highlight shadow and their edge transfers reveal form and texture
research_limitations: the handbook teaches controllable production lighting and does not guarantee that a generated image reveals the actual fixture
source size must be understood relative to subject distance and scene geometry
reuse_note: Own hard and soft light through shadow-edge and specular relations; keep fixture names in a setup-candidate lane.

abstracted_dimensions: loop nose shadow remains separate from cheek shadow
Rembrandt nose and cheek shadow relation leaves a contained far-cheek light triangle
split and butterfly patterns use distinct face-axis and nose-shadow geometry
research_limitations: a manufacturer tutorial is a practical secondary source rather than a controlled perception study
face shape pose fill and source height can change the apparent pattern
reuse_note: Encode the nose-cheek connection and centered-shadow relations, not the pattern names alone.

abstracted_dimensions: broad lighting illuminates the face side that presents more area to the camera
face turn and lit-side relationship are jointly required
modifier changes softness without changing broad-side ownership
research_limitations: the page demonstrates broad lighting more directly than short lighting
head rotation and camera position must remain readable in the final frame
reuse_note: Treat broad and short as camera-face-light orientation relations, never as left-light versus right-light labels.

abstracted_dimensions: small straight-on flash produces hard crisp shadows
low ambient exposure can leave a dark background while the near subject is strongly flash-lit
bounce or a larger acting source broadens shadow transitions
research_limitations: the product tutorial does not define a universal Y2K aesthetic
straight-on flash can also serve as daylight fill and therefore needs a visible ambient and shadow relation
reuse_note: Own direct-flash pixels through near-axis hard-shadow and subject-background exposure relations; keep Y2K candidate-only.

abstracted_dimensions: white balance can neutralize a cast or be used creatively
mixed lighting can contain incompatible source colors
a neutral reference supports correction but does not reveal the original source by itself
research_limitations: white-balance metadata and raw sensor response are not recoverable from generated pixels
warm material color and warm grading can imitate source color
reuse_note: Require spatially distinct source zones for mixed light and never infer CCT or WB settings from appearance.

abstracted_dimensions: CTO CTB and CTS alter source color in different correction directions
plusgreen and minusgreen address green-magenta source mismatch
neutral-density filtration changes transmission without defining a color look
research_limitations: a photographed color cast cannot identify a specific filter product or density
filter transmission varies by product and source spectrum
reuse_note: Preserve explicit filter requests as setup metadata and translate them to a bounded color result without claiming the filter is visible.

abstracted_dimensions: colour rendering index compares rendering under a test illuminant with a reference illuminant
the metric is a measurement rather than a photographic style label
appearance alone does not reveal the test conditions or exact index
research_limitations: CRI does not summarize every color-fidelity or camera-response concern
a generated image has no measured test illuminant
reuse_note: Keep CRI Ra and R9 outside hard visual semantics; retain only when the requester explicitly supplies them.

abstracted_dimensions: legacy CRI has known limits for accurate scientific fidelity evaluation
a single quality number does not own all color preference or fidelity dimensions
measurement purpose and reference conditions matter
research_limitations: the publication addresses measurement methodology rather than photographic prompt design
color fidelity and aesthetic preference remain separate
reuse_note: Do not translate a high color-quality score into generic beautiful skin or saturated color candidates.

abstracted_dimensions: TLCI evaluates luminaire colorimetric performance through a camera-oriented model
the result depends on defined test and reference conditions
TLCI is not a directly visible style
research_limitations: the recommendation does not validate arbitrary camera or grading pipelines
generated pixels cannot prove the measured luminaire
reuse_note: Store explicit TLCI as technical metadata only.

abstracted_dimensions: SSI measures spectral similarity between a test source and a chosen reference
the metric is grounded in spectral power distributions
different references can yield different similarity results
research_limitations: SSI does not by itself predict every photographed color after camera processing
a rendered image contains no source SPD measurement
reuse_note: Keep SSI and SPD outside visual-profile activation and candidate aesthetic scoring.

abstracted_dimensions: point-source illuminance falls with the square of distance
finite-source geometry limits simple near-field application
distance anchors are necessary to interpret visible falloff
research_limitations: real scenes include extended sources reflections exposure and tone mapping
pixels cannot establish an exact lux or stop ratio without calibrated capture data
reuse_note: Translate falloff into relative subject-background brightness and distance relations; do not promise exact inverse-square measurement.

abstracted_dimensions: exposure highlights shadows whites and blacks are distinct tone controls
curve editing changes tonal mapping
color grading can tint shadows midtones and highlights independently
grain clarity dehaze and clipping are separate effects or diagnostics
research_limitations: software controls describe edit operations and do not prove how an image was captured
many different edits can converge on similar pixels
reuse_note: Keep lighting ownership and postprocess ownership separate even when a final candidate pack combines them.

abstracted_dimensions: anti-halation structures reduce light piping and halo around strong exposure
halation is related to light scattering within film support and layers
film processing and stock structure are causal conditions beyond visible style alone
research_limitations: a digital effect can imitate the visible halo without film capture
the exact color and width vary by stock exposure processing and scan
reuse_note: Name the profile a film-halation look and require a thin localized highlight-edge halo; never infer a real stock or process.

abstracted_dimensions: bleach bypass retains silver and changes contrast shadow density and saturation
the process belongs to film processing rather than scene illumination
a similar digital grade does not prove the chemical process
research_limitations: the visible result depends on stock exposure lab procedure and transfer
a generated image can represent only a bleach-bypass look
reuse_note: Keep bleach bypass candidate-only and label it as a look unless the requester supplies process metadata.

abstracted_dimensions: lens-surface reflections can form displaced ghost images
scattered internal reflection can create haze and lower contrast
coatings reduce but do not turn all flare manifestations into one visual type
research_limitations: the technical article discusses physical optics rather than generated-image review
digital overlays can imitate ghosts without optical causality
reuse_note: Split aligned ghost images from broad veiling contrast loss and hold halation in a different film-response profile.

abstracted_dimensions: small apertures can produce diffraction spikes around bright point sources
spike form relates to aperture blades
a starburst is not a flare ghost or painted star shape
research_limitations: the article gives a practical technique rather than a universal diffraction model
pixels do not identify the exact f-number or lens
reuse_note: Keep starburst candidate-only in this iteration and separate it from flare and halation vocabulary.

abstracted_dimensions: light-dark tonal contrast can model three-dimensional form
the method can create dramatic effect
chiaroscuro is more specific than a dark background or contrast increase
research_limitations: an art glossary spans painting traditions and does not define a single photographic setup
stylistic attribution remains broader than a pixel contract
reuse_note: Own the profile through directional form modeling and connected midtones; keep historical style labels optional.

abstracted_dimensions: strong highlights are set against a predominantly dark field
the effect is more extreme than ordinary chiaroscuro
illumination creates a concentrated hierarchy within darkness
research_limitations: tenebrism is an art-historical term with variable use
a vignette or global underexposure can imitate darkness without selective illumination
reuse_note: Require a dominant dark field plus isolated coherent light pool and preserved local structure.

abstracted_dimensions: film noir classification exceeds one lighting recipe
genre identity also involves narrative psychology setting and historical framing
high-contrast or low-key light is only a partial visual signature
research_limitations: the article addresses genre boundaries rather than lighting measurement
no single still establishes all noir genre properties
reuse_note: Keep noir as a candidate cluster and harden only its separately named lighting relations such as gobo pool silhouette or low-key.

abstracted_dimensions: motivated and unmotivated lighting are creative choices rather than a quality hierarchy
psychological lighting can depart from literal visible-source motivation
motivation must be judged through scene-specific source ownership
research_limitations: production commentary does not prescribe one universal motivated-light geometry
a frame can make a source plausible without proving the actual off-camera fixture
reuse_note: Require visible source and coherent direction color falloff while describing the relation as visually motivated, not physically proven.

abstracted_dimensions: a visible practical can be augmented by another production unit
the augmenting unit should support the practical's apparent direction and role
the photographed effect need not be produced by the visible lamp alone
research_limitations: one production example cannot define all practical-light scenes
actual fixture ownership remains behind-the-scenes metadata
reuse_note: Encode apparent spatial motivation and never require the visible practical to be the literal sole emitter.

abstracted_dimensions: golden and blue hours occupy different solar-elevation and twilight relationships
golden hour often combines low warm direct light with long shadows
blue hour emphasizes cool ambient twilight and can balance artificial practical light
research_limitations: the precise duration and appearance vary by latitude season weather and obstruction
warm or cool grading alone does not establish the time
reuse_note: Own visible low-sun and twilight-practical relations, not actual clock time or geographic conditions.

abstracted_dimensions: crepuscular rays require light scattering through the atmosphere
occluding cloud or terrain structures create alternating bright and shadowed paths
perspective can make near-parallel rays appear to diverge
research_limitations: the source concerns atmospheric-scale rays and not every studio haze setup
a flare streak or painted beam can imitate a ray without source-occluder-medium continuity
reuse_note: Require a visible source direction occluder scattering medium and receiving surface relation for volumetric shafts.

abstracted_dimensions: longer atmospheric paths near the horizon preferentially remove shorter wavelengths from direct sunlight
aerosols clouds and atmospheric state alter observed sunset color
red-orange color alone is not a time-of-day proof
research_limitations: atmospheric color varies and is not guaranteed at every sunset
generated pixels cannot reveal the actual aerosol or weather state
reuse_note: Use warm low-angle direct light with geometry and shadow evidence; reject a global warm grade as sufficient.
